newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares higher, Leykam takes a knock.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares higher, Leykam takes a knock.

text.p: Austrian shares ended a see-saw session 0.56 percent up, shrugging off a sell-off in paper maker Leykam that came after the firm's Dutch parent announced it was halting investment in its paper producing unit.
The ATX index of 21 blue chip shares closed at 1,048.81 points -- 5.84 up on the day and 8.99 off the session low.
Traders forecast a test of resistance at 1,050 points in the coming week. "The market will have no trouble holding above 1,040 points," one said.
Steel firm VA Stahl was among the day's top gainers in brisk trade, rising 12 schillings to 371.

Dealers said the stock had benefited from the firm's decision to change its financial year, bringing a possible windfall in 1997/8 when the government will reinstate tax breaks on losses carried forward.
"There were two big buy orders and that turned VA Stahl into a high flyer," a trader said.

The day's biggest loser was Leykam-Muerztaler. Its shares slumped 15 schillings, or 4.69 percent, to 305 schillings after Dutch KNP BT, which controls 72 percent of the paper firm, said it was abandoning investment in KNP Leykam.
Leykam-Muerztaler has a 30 percent stake in KNP Leykam.
"News of the investment stop has hardly been greeted with euphoria," a trader said.
"Not investing stands for neglecting," said another.
National utility Verbund dipped six schillings to 746 on high turnover. Traders pinpointed foreign selling and said further losses may be in store.
The broad based Vienna bourse index closed 0.71 points up at 405.6. October ATX futures were 6.0 points up at 1,053.0. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
